root_causes: followers table lacked tenant_id constraint which allowed cross-tenant links
Missing composite uniqueness allowed duplicate relationships under concurrency
Redis cache was updated without coordination with DB causing drift on failures
Transactions were not shard-aware; no retry logic for IntegrityError or deadlocks
Soft deletes were not excluded from queries and cache invalidation
refactored_schema_changes: Added 'tenant_id' to followers table and composite uniqueness constraint (tenant_id, follower_id, followed_id)
Added 'deleted' soft-delete boolean to followers table and excluded deleted from relationship queries
Added validation hook to prevent cross-tenant relationships
transaction_isolation_and_sharding: Implemented ShardManager to map tenant->DB shard and provide session_scope with retries
Implemented coordinated_commit simulation with sequential commit and rollback on failure (simulate 2PC)
cache_consistency: Implemented versioned write-through cache (`VersionedCounter`) backed by FakeRedis for tests
Implemented lock-based updates to prevent duplicate writes and ensure recent versions win
Added drift_monitor to compare DB and cache counts per tenant and user
soft_delete_sync: Soft-deleted rows marked deleted=True are excluded from follower queries
Added tests to ensure cache doesn't count soft-deleted relationships
Cleanup strategy: periodic drift_monitor + background job can remove soft-deleted rows older than threshold
notes: Two-phase commit is simulated in tests; production requires a real 2PC coordinator or distributed transaction manager for cross-shard atomicity
Redis lock is a naive implementation; replace with a robust algorithm (e.g., Redlock library) and use a real Redis cluster in production
Add scheduled jobs to run `drift_monitor` every X minutes to reconcile counts
Consider storing a canonical follower_count on users table updated inside DB transactions and using write-through cache for read performance
